headline: Trishal UNO Arafat Siddique withdrawn after slapping worker
summary: The Upazila Nirbahi Officer was transferred to the Ministry of Public Administration following a viral CCTV video showing him assaulting a worker and a RAB member.
details: Arafat Siddique, the Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) of Trishal in Mymensingh, has been withdrawn and attached to the Ministry of Public Administration.
The action follows a viral CCTV video from Wednesday afternoon at a sand sale point in the Kulurbari area of Kathal Union.
The footage shows the UNO slapping a worker twice—first with his left hand and then with his right.
The video further reveals that when a RAB member tried to intervene and take the worker away, the UNO took a stick from the member and struck him four times.
An Assistant Commissioner (Land) reportedly tried to stop the UNO during the incident.
Following the incident, the UNO was absent from his office on Thursday, leaving many service seekers without assistance.
A reconciliation meeting was later held at a local hospital, initiated by MP Mahbubur Rahman and attended by local BNP leaders and the victim's associates.
During the meeting, Arafat Siddique expressed regret for his actions, stating that the incident happened suddenly during lawful activities.
caption:
A viral video showing a UNO slapping a worker and striking a RAB member with a stick has led to his immediate withdrawal.

Arafat Siddique, the Upazila Nirbahi Officer (UNO) of Trishal in Mymensingh, has been withdrawn and attached to the Ministry of Public Administration.

The action follows a viral CCTV video from Wednesday afternoon at a sand sale point in the Kulurbari area of Kathal Union.

The footage shows the UNO slapping a worker twice—first with his left hand and then with his right.

The video further reveals that when a RAB member tried to intervene and take the worker away, the UNO took a stick from the member and struck him four times.

An Assistant Commissioner (Land) reportedly tried to stop the UNO during the incident.

Following the incident, the UNO was absent from his office on Thursday, leaving many service seekers without assistance.

A reconciliation meeting was later held at a local hospital, initiated by MP Mahbubur Rahman and attended by local BNP leaders and the victim's associates.

During the meeting, Arafat Siddique expressed regret for his actions, stating that the incident happened suddenly during lawful activities.

headline_marked: Hasan Mahmud's 6-55 as [[Bangladesh bowl Australia out for 198]] in Darwin
headline: Hasan Mahmud's 6-55 as Bangladesh bowl Australia out for 198 in Darwin
summary: Hasan Mahmud claims a career-best haul to dismantle Australia on Day 1, leaving the Tigers in a strong position with a 96-1 start in their first innings.
details: Hasan Mahmud delivered a masterclass in bowling, taking 6-55 to bowl Australia out for 198 on the first day of the Test in Darwin. This marks Hasan's career-best Test figures and the third-best innings haul by any Bangladesh pacer.

With this performance, Hasan became the first Bangladesh bowler to take a five-wicket haul in Australia across all formats. He has now achieved three Test five-fors, all occurring in away matches against Pakistan, India, and Australia.
Australia's total of 198 is their lowest ever Test score against Bangladesh, surpassing the previous low of 217 recorded during the 2017 Mirpur Test.

In a rare feat, Bangladesh's pacers took all 10 wickets in the innings, only the second time this has happened in Test history for the Tigers, following a similar achievement against Pakistan in 2024.
Bangladesh responded strongly, closing the day at 96-1. Mominul Haque remained unbeaten on 35, while Tanzid Hasan contributed 32 runs.
Mominul Haque also reached a milestone, surpassing Tamim Iqbal (5,134) to become Bangladesh's second-highest Test run-scorer, trailing only Mushfiqur Rahim.
For Australia, Steve Smith joined Steve Waugh at the top of the list for the most fifty-plus scores for Australia with his 82nd such innings.
Mitchell Starc also made history, becoming the most successful left-arm bowler in Test history with 434 wickets, surpassing Sri Lanka's Rangana Herath.
caption:
Hasan Mahmud's career-best 6-55 destroys Australia for 198! 🇧🇩

Hasan Mahmud delivered a masterclass in bowling, taking 6-55 to bowl Australia out for 198 on the first day of the Test in Darwin. This marks Hasan's career-best Test figures and the third-best innings haul by any Bangladesh pacer.

With this performance, Hasan became the first Bangladesh bowler to take a five-wicket haul in Australia across all formats. He has now achieved three Test five-fors, all occurring in away matches against Pakistan, India, and Australia.

Australia's total of 198 is their lowest ever Test score against Bangladesh, surpassing the previous low of 217 recorded during the 2017 Mirpur Test.

In a rare feat, Bangladesh's pacers took all 10 wickets in the innings, only the second time this has happened in Test history for the Tigers, following a similar achievement against Pakistan in 2024.

Bangladesh responded strongly, closing the day at 96-1. Mominul Haque remained unbeaten on 35, while Tanzid Hasan contributed 32 runs.

Mominul Haque also reached a milestone, surpassing Tamim Iqbal (5,134) to become Bangladesh's second-highest Test run-scorer, trailing only Mushfiqur Rahim.

For Australia, Steve Smith joined Steve Waugh at the top of the list for the most fifty-plus scores for Australia with his 82nd such innings.

Mitchell Starc also made history, becoming the most successful left-arm bowler in Test history with 434 wickets, surpassing Sri Lanka's Rangana Herath.
